alignments.note: The ASV opens the verse bare, writing no connective for the waw; unrepresented under rule 14's closing sentences.

Supplied subject pronoun. No nominal standing in this verse denotes the referent (the ruler of v.3), and rule 10 makes the verse the whole unit of work, so rule 25's resumption does not reach it: added under rule 20's closing sentence, on the terms rule 17 gives a supplied lexical subject.

Comparative kaph heading the predicate of a verbless clause; the construction-supplied copula joins the preposition and the unit heads on it under rule 49. Discontinuous only in that the copula precedes the preposition.

Construct noun with a supplied *the* under rule 29; no article morpheme stands anywhere in the chain, and the ASV writes a determiner before each of the two English nouns, so each noun takes the one standing before its own word.
Nomen rectum with the chain's *of* under rule 19, plus the second supplied *the* standing before its own word (rule 29's counting).
Supplied subordinator over a clause the Hebrew writes asyndetically — no conjunction morpheme stands in `יִזְרַח שָׁמֶשׁ` — so added under rule 55.
Subject noun with a supplied definite article under rule 15; no article morpheme is segmented here, the bracketed gloss notwithstanding.
Finite verb rendered by its lexical verb alone; the subject noun stands written, so nothing else joins it under rule 17.
Indefinite article belongs to the noun that licenses it under rule 15.

The negative takes the *without* the ASV writes for it. The noun keeps its own English word, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is unmet and rule 2 splits the pair rather than fusing them as rule 35 fuses a single negative word carrying both morphemes.
Noun with its own English word.

Supplied subordinator over a verbless clause with no conjunction morpheme in it; added under rule 55. It is a separate unit from the supplied *springeth* because the ASV's own rendered material (*the tender grass*) stands between the two runs, as rule 2 directs.

One substantive rendered by a multi-word phrase with a supplied determiner (rule 15). Head under rule 31's tie-reading: the ASV writes a bare *grass* for other Hebrew words of that class, so *grass* realizes the lexeme and *tender* is the specifier. The competing reading heads on *tender*, taking *grass* as a supplied generic as in *high place*.

Supplied lexical verb for a clause whose Hebrew writes none (`דֶּשֶׁא מֵאָרֶץ`); no morpheme is there to carry it, so added under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause and rule 34. The ASV italic corroborates and decides nothing, by rule 7.
Ablative `מִן` rendered by a two-word English preposition, headed on the word carrying the lexeme under rule 24.
Noun with a supplied definite article under rule 15; no article morpheme is segmented.
`מִן` rendered *Through*; the ASV reorders this colon after the `דֶּשֶׁא` colon, which rule 25 allows.
One substantive rendered by a two-word phrase; *shining* carries the lexeme of `נֹגַהּ` and *clear* is the ASV's supplied modifier, so the head goes on *shining* under rule 31's subtraction test.
`מִן` rendered *after*; the word the ASV writes for the relation is the preposition's under rule 11.
Noun with its own English word.

review_notes: The ASV reorders the verse's last two cola: the Hebrew writes `מִנֹּגַהּ מִמָּטָר` before `דֶּשֶׁא מֵאָרֶץ`, while the English writes *Through clear shining after rain* last. Units are ordered by the source here; rule 25 allows the reordering.
Two supplied English runs are marked `added` in the third colon (*When* and *springeth*), kept separate because the ASV's own rendering of `דֶּשֶׁא` stands between them.
*He* is `added` rather than resumptive: the referent is named in v.3, not in this verse, and rule 10 makes the verse the whole unit of work.
